content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves a chain-against-chain collision by noting that the challenger's footed chain does not name Joseph, which is a verse-level naming requirement the rule retires in favor of footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side. A link is judged by its support, never by whether any verse, or the chain as a whole, states it word for word; and a verse whose words leave the question open decides nothing by itself.","room":"by footing, never verse by verse: I weighed whether the judge compared the chains' footing as wholes or instead required explicit naming, a verse-by-verse or word-for-word test.","why":"The judge makes a footed chain underdetermined partly because it does not explicitly name Joseph, using a word-for-word or verse-level test rather than chain-against-chain footing, so the text breaches K-C."}
